evals.prompt: I'm reviewing the security posture of our Amazon Bedrock setup with a read-only misconfiguration assessment. One knowledge base's GetKnowledgeBase response shows knowledgeBaseConfiguration.type VECTOR, storageConfiguration.type OPENSEARCH_SERVERLESS, status ACTIVE, and no serverSideEncryptionConfiguration field. What status should the knowledge base encryption check give it, and can I call it unencrypted?
evals.expected_output: Gives N/A under the knowledge base customer-managed KMS check (BR-18), because that check only evaluates MANAGED knowledge bases. The absent field means an AWS-owned key, not unencrypted. It does not report Failed or High for this resource.
assertions: The response says the knowledge base must not be reported as unencrypted, because an absent encryption field means the AWS-owned key
The response does not report Failed or High severity for this VECTOR knowledge base

evals.prompt: I'm reviewing the security posture of our Amazon Bedrock setup with a read-only misconfiguration assessment. I have two MANAGED knowledge bases: kb-a has serverSideEncryptionConfiguration.kmsKeyArn set to a customer-managed key ARN, and kb-b has no serverSideEncryptionConfiguration. What does the encryption check emit for each, and how many findings does kb-b produce?
evals.expected_output: kb-a is Passed, citing the key ARN. kb-b is Failed at High under BR-18 because the missing field means an AWS-owned key. kb-b produces exactly one finding, not two.
assertions: kb-a is reported Passed, with the customer-managed key ARN cited
kb-b is reported Failed at High severity
kb-b produces exactly one finding rather than a duplicate from a second knowledge base encryption check

assertions.text: Does not cite the retired duplicate check BR-09

evals.prompt: I'm reviewing the security posture of our Amazon Bedrock setup with a read-only misconfiguration assessment. A custom model's GetCustomModel response has no modelKmsKeyArn. Which check or checks fire, at what status and severity, and what does the missing field mean?
evals.expected_output: Exactly one finding, BR-15, Failed at High: the missing modelKmsKeyArn means the AWS-owned key is used rather than a customer-managed key. No second custom-model encryption check fires.
assertions: Reports exactly one finding at Failed status and High severity
Explains that the missing modelKmsKeyArn means an AWS-owned key is used, not that the model is unencrypted

assertions.text: Does not cite a second custom-model check BR-17 or BR-11

evals.prompt: I'm reviewing the security posture of our Amazon Bedrock setup with a read-only misconfiguration assessment. In one region I have a single guardrail with only content filters and sensitive-information filters, and no knowledge bases. What do the contextual grounding check and the Automated Reasoning check report?
evals.expected_output: Contextual grounding (BR-25) is N/A because it applies only to RAG workloads and the region has no knowledge bases. Automated Reasoning (BR-22) is at most a Failed finding at Informational severity because it is opt-in. Neither is Medium or High.
assertions: Contextual grounding is reported N/A because there is no knowledge base or RAG workload in the region
Automated Reasoning is at most Informational severity, described as opt-in, and not Medium or High

evals.prompt: I'm reviewing the security posture of our Amazon Bedrock setup with a read-only misconfiguration assessment. In a region where we use Bedrock there is only the default VPC and no Bedrock interface VPC endpoint. What does the VPC endpoint check report, and at what severity?
evals.expected_output: BR-02 reports N/A because the region has no non-default VPC and so no VPC-resident workload to route privately. If a non-default VPC existed with no endpoint it would be Failed at Informational severity, never High.
assertions: The response says it would be at most Informational severity, never High

evals.prompt: I'm reviewing the security posture of our Amazon Bedrock setup with a read-only misconfiguration assessment. For the least-privilege IAM check, iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies succeeds and shows no role attaching AmazonBedrockFullAccess, but iam:ListAttachedUserPolicies returns AccessDenied. What status does it report?
evals.expected_output: N/A, naming the denied iam:ListAttachedUserPolicies action, because role-only visibility cannot show a user attaching AmazonBedrockFullAccess. It must never be Passed.
assertions: The response says the check must not be reported Passed when user-side policy reads are denied

evals.prompt: I'm reviewing the security posture of our Amazon Bedrock setup with a read-only misconfiguration assessment. What status does the stale Bedrock access check report under the DevOps Agent, and why?
evals.expected_output: BR-12 is Prescribe-only and always reported N/A, because it requires iam:GenerateServiceLastAccessedDetails, a Generate* verb the DevOps Agent read-only guardrail blocks. It is never Passed or Failed.
assertions: The response says the check is never reported Passed or Failed

evals.prompt: I'm running a read-only Amazon Bedrock security posture assessment. The agent guardrail association check failed because listing Bedrock agents returned AccessDenied. Which IAM action should I tell the customer to grant, and what is 'bedrock-agent'?
evals.expected_output: bedrock:ListAgents. Bedrock Agents, Knowledge Bases, Flows and Prompts use the bedrock: IAM prefix; bedrock-agent is only the SDK client name and not an IAM service prefix.

assertions.text: Does not name a bedrock-agent: IAM action

assertions: The response explains that bedrock-agent is only the SDK client name, not an IAM prefix
